## Declarations and implementations

```plato

    //==
    // # Algebra operations
    //
    // Derived functionality for the elementary operation interfaces
    // (`algebra.concepts.plato`): powers, the named scalar fractions and
    // multiples, and the interpolation helpers built on `Lerp`
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_interpolation). Shared provenance note:
    // `core.library.plato`.

    //==
    // IAdditive

    // The value added to itself: x + x. (Name overlaps C#'s Double type; unambiguous
    // here as a method and worth keeping for the additive-doubling idiom.)
    Double(x: IAdditive): IAdditive
        => x + x;

    //==
    // IMultiplicative

    // The value multiplied by itself: x * x.
    Square(x: IMultiplicative): IMultiplicative
        => x * x;

    // The value raised to the third power: x * x * x.
    Cube(x: IMultiplicative): IMultiplicative
        => x * x * x;

    // The value raised to the fourth power.
    Pow4(x: IMultiplicative): IMultiplicative
        => x.Square.Square;

    // The value raised to the fifth power.
    Pow5(x: IMultiplicative): IMultiplicative
        => x.Square.Square * x;

    //==
    // IInvertible
    //
    // No derivations: Inverse is the sole member and every useful combination
    // (e.g. a/b as a * b.Inverse) requires IMultiplicative, which IInvertible does
    // not inherit. Types that are both (IReal via IArithmetic) get division directly.

    //==
    // IScalable

    // Half of x (divides by two).
    Half(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 2.0;

    // One third of x (divides by three).
    Third(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 3.0;

    // One quarter of x (divides by four).
    Quarter(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 4.0;

    // One eighth of x.
    Eighth(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 8.0;

    // One sixteenth of x.
    Sixteenth(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 16.0;

    // One tenth of x.
    Tenth(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 10.0;

    // One hundredth of x.
    Hundredth(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 100.0;

    // One thousandth of x.
    Thousandth(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 1000.0;

    // One millionth of x.
    Millionth(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 1000000.0;

    // One billionth of x (short-scale billion, 1e9).
    Billionth(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x / 1000000000.0;

    // A million times x.
    Million(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x * 1000000.0;

    // A billion times x (short-scale billion, 1e9).
    Billion(x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x * 1000000000.0;

    // Scales x by the given percentage (100 yields x unchanged).
    Percent(x: IScalable, percent: Number): IScalable
        => x * (percent / 100.0);

    // Scalar-on-the-left multiplication, so `2.0 * v` reads as well as `v * 2.0`.
    // Delegates to the IScalable member; adds no new semantics.
    Multiply(scalar: Number, x: IScalable): IScalable
        => x * scalar;

    //==
    // IInterpolatable

    // The midpoint between a and b (linear interpolation at t = 0.5).
    MidPoint(a: IInterpolatable, b: IInterpolatable): IInterpolatable
        => a.Lerp(b, 0.5);

    // Linear interpolation with the parameter t clamped to [0, 1], so the result
    // never extrapolates beyond the a..b segment.
    LerpClamped(a: IInterpolatable, b: IInterpolatable, t: Number): IInterpolatable
        => a.Lerp(b, t.Saturate);

    // Interpolates from a to b with smoothstep easing: the parameter t is reshaped
    // by the weight t*t*(3 - 2*t), giving zero slope at both ends for a gentle
    // start and stop. Requested cross-package by P3 (ICoordinate). Assumes t in [0,1].
    SmoothLerp(a: IInterpolatable, b: IInterpolatable, t: Number): IInterpolatable
        => a.Lerp(b, t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t));
}
```
